headline: Kings’ Quinton Byfield exits game with upper-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Kings forward Quinton Byfield left Tuesday's game with an upper-body injury. He has two points so far this season, and LAK entered the night as the NHL's only winless team.

The numbers suggest Byfield has been better than his line. His five-on-five expected goals share, the portion of chance quality LAK gets while he's on the ice, is 63.63%, and the team does 18.97 percentage points better in that measure with him out there. His own expected goals total is 1.87 against one actual goal, so he is about 0.87 goals short of what his chances warranted so far this season. That points toward a scoring dip that should correct, which makes the injury more costly. LAK as a whole sits at 1-4-2, with a goals saved above expected of -6.8 (goaltending has cost them nearly seven goals relative to the shots faced), so they can't easily absorb losing a driver.

If he misses time, the minutes are going by how the coach has used his players, not by games already played without him. Scott Laughton (14:40 a night) is next in line for his ice time, and Alex Turcotte, the busiest man on the second power-play unit, is the likeliest to move up.
